en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Seventh Chapter
The Discourse on What is Given Here: Is it the case that by what is given here they maintain themselves there?
Yes, it is.
"Do they give robe-cloth from here and use that robe-cloth there?
"One should not say so. ...pe...

"They give almsfood from here, they give lodgings from here, they give medicinal requisites for the sick from here, they give solid food from here, they give soft food from here, they give drinking water from here;"
"Is that water consumed there?
"One should not say so... "...Pe...
Is it by means of what is given from here that they maintain themselves there?"
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “Is it the case that one person is the doer of another’s action, and that one person creates the pleasure and pain of another, while another experiences them?
“One should certainly not say so…” [and so on].
Is it not to be said that "by what is given here, they maintain themselves there"?
Yes, it is.
Is it not the case that the departed (petas) rejoice when someone gives a gift for their own benefit, clear their minds, experience rapture, and obtain gladness?
Yes, they do.
Since the departed rejoice when someone gives a gift for their own benefit, clear their minds, experience rapture, and obtain gladness;
Therefore, indeed, it should be said:
"By what is given here, they maintain themselves there.
It should not be said [otherwise].
“Is it not the case that they maintain themselves there by what is given from here?”—
“Yes.
But was it not said by the Blessed One:
“Just as water that has rained upon a height flows downward along its course,
even so what is given from here [flows]— ”
It is beneficial for the departed.
Just as rivers full of water fill the ocean;
In the same way, what is given from here benefits the departed;
for there is no agriculture there.
In this [work], there is no tending of cattle;
there is no such trade as buying and selling with gold.
"Those deceased, departed spirits live there on what is given from here.
Is this indeed a sutta?
“Yes,” [you say].
“In that case, it must not be said that ‘by what is given here, they maintain themselves there’.”
“Is it not the case that they maintain themselves there by what is given from here?”—
“Yes.”—
“Has it not been said by the Blessed One:”
“Bhikkhus, seeing five grounds, parents desire a son to be born into their family. What are the five? He will support us when we are old;
he will perform our duties; the lineage of the family will endure for long; he will take charge of the inheritance; or else, he will provide offerings for the deceased who have passed away.”
"Monks, seeing these five reasons, mothers and fathers desire a son to be born into their family.
Seeing five reasons,
the wise desire a son."
Either a warrior will support us,
or he will perform our service;
thus the lineage of the family will endure for a long time.
He partakes of the inheritance,
or else he will offer a sacrificial gift for the sake of the departed.
Seeing these advantages,
the wise desire a son;
therefore, virtuous and noble persons—
Grateful and mindful of what has been done for them,
they support their mother and father,
recollecting what was done for them in the past.
They perform services for them,
as is fitting for those who have acted as benefactors; one who follows advice and supports his master—
Without bringing ruin to his family lineage,
endowed with faith and perfected in virtue,
such a son is worthy of praise.”
Is that indeed the Sutta? Yes.
Therefore, they maintain themselves there by what is given from here.
The discourse on what has been given is finished.
